pageCache.text:
PE and Sports Premium
Sports Premium Expenditure 2024-2025

Wraparound Care
Funtington Primary School Wrapround Club offers breakfast and after school care to children in our school from Reception class to Year 6 every day in term time.
Breakfast Club opens at 07:45 and runs until classrooms open at 08:40.
Children are offered a selection of breakfast items such as cereal, toast and porridge along with fruit and juice.
After School Club runs from 15:20 until 18:00. Parents have the option to book an early finish at 16:30 for a reduced price.
Children are offered a snack immediately after school before taking part in a range of activities. They then sit together to have a light meal at about 16:45 before continuing to play until parents arrive. Collection from the club can happen at any time between 15:30 and 18:00.
Breakfast Club costs £5 per session.
After School Club costs £12 per session or £6 for an early finish at 16:30.
We can accept Childcare Vouchers and Tax-Free Childcare payments.
For more information, or to make a booking please email wrap@funtingtonprimaryschool.co.uk
Wraparound Care Policy

The Governing Board
School governors are volunteers who work as a team, alongside the Headteacher to set the vision, aims and policies of the school. Their primary aim is long-term vision and accountability, with the Headteacher responsible for day-to-day mangement.
The governing board has three core functions:
Please use the following links for more information about our Governors
Governor Biographies
Governor Impact Statement 2025-2026
The governing board at Funtington Primary School have been pleased to continue to play a key role in supporting the school to thrive over the past year. Building on the positive feedback from Ofsted inspectors, the governors have continued to work strategically alongside school staff to preserve our school ethos, champion pupil wellbeing and safety, and continue to promote a love of learning.
This year, the board supported the full implementation of the Outdoor Play and Learning (OPAL) programme, which is still being built upon. This programme is designed to provide an inclusive and engaging play environment, contributing to every pupil’s personal development and enjoyment of school life. Governors allocated funding to transform our school grounds and positively impact the playtime experience for all pupils, including the most disadvantaged and vulnerable.
To support our families, we approved a revised financial model for our school-led Breakfast and After-School Wraparound Care Programme, ensuring its ongoing sustainability. The new model allows greater flexibility, allowing more families to use the provision.
Using data and observations from the Headteacher’s reports, the board actively challenged and supported school leaders in the implementation of the school’s development priorities. This included monitoring lead subjects, approving the funding for resources and staff training, and restructuring roles to address senior leadership workloads and promote staff progression.
Meeting every month during the school year, the board ensures that every strategic decision benefits our pupils, staff, and the wider community, promoting a culture of aspiration for all of our pupils rooted in the Funtington Footprints.
If you are interested in joining our governing board, please contact our Chair, Mr Michael Gauntlett by email: chairofgovernors@funtingtonprimaryschool.co.uk

Curriculum
At Funtington Primary School, our curriculum is designed to embody the aims of our school vision: confidence, community, success, learning and caring. We strive to create an inclusive community where every child feels a strong sense of belonging, is valued for their unique strengths, and is supported to achieve their personal best.
Our curriculum aims to nurture enthusiastic learners who feel happy, safe, and proud of their successes. We believe in developing the whole child, fostering not just academic progress, but also their social, emotional, and physical wellbeing. Through a carefully sequenced and coherent programme of study, and a broad range of experiences within and beyond the classroom, we equip our pupils with the knowledge, skills, and understanding to be well-prepared for the next phase of their education and beyond.
Underpinning our curriculum is a firm commitment to developing curious, independent thinkers who have the skills and attitudes to continue learning throughout their lives. The unique context of our school and its setting, its connection to the surrounding area and local community provides a wealth of learning experiences that enable our pupils to develop their sense of place and identity and serves to enrich our curriculum.
By providing a curriculum that is broad, balanced and personalised to our school, taught alongside our core values of the Funtington Footprints, we aim for our pupils to develop a genuine enjoyment of learning that allows them to ‘Move Forward, Loving Learning’.

pageCache.pageTitle: Funtington Primary School - Mental Health & Wellbeing
pageCache.text:
Mental Health & Wellbeing
At our school, we believe that mental health is just as important as physical health. Children who feel safe, supported, and valued are better able to learn, build friendships, and enjoy school life.
We place wellbeing at the heart of everything we do through a whole-school approach, ensuring every child feels included, understood, and ready to thrive.
What is Mental Health?
Mental health is about how we think, feel, and behave. It affects how children:
Cope with challenges
Engage with learning
All children experience ups and downs. Our role is to help them develop the confidence, resilience, and emotional skills they need to navigate these successfully.
How We Support Children in School
We provide a consistent and embedded approach to wellbeing across all areas of school life. This is not a one-off initiative, but part of our daily practice and culture.
Our approach includes:
A safe, caring and inclusive environment where every child feels they belong
Trusted adults who listen and respond to children’s needs
Teaching of social and emotional skills through our curriculum
Opportunities for pupil voice, so children feel heard and valued
Early identification of needs and timely support
Targeted interventions for children who need additional help
Strong partnerships with families and external services
Through this, we aim to develop pupils’ emotional wellbeing, resilience, and readiness to learn.
Recognising When a Child May Need Support
Every child is different, but you may notice:
Changes in mood or behaviour
Increased anxiety or withdrawal
Difficulty with friendships
Changes in sleep or appetite
Physical complaints such as headaches or tummy aches
Reduced engagement in school or learning
If you notice any of these signs, early support can make a big difference. Please speak to us - we are here to help.
Working Together with Parents & Carers
We know that children do best when school and home work in partnership.
Keep you informed about your child’s wellbeing
Listen to your concerns and work together on solutions
Offer practical advice and strategies
Signpost you to additional support where needed
If you have any concerns, please contact your child’s class teacher or a member of the leadership team.
Supporting Your Child at Home
There are simple ways you can support your child’s mental health:
Talk and listen regularly without judgement
Keep routines to provide stability and security
Encourage play, relaxation, and physical activity
Help children name and understand their feelings
Spend quality time together
Model positive ways of coping with challenges
These small steps help children build resilience and emotional confidence over time.
Support for Families
Sometimes extra support is needed, and that’s okay. The following organisations offer trusted advice and guidance:
YoungMinds – support for children and parents
NSPCC – advice on children’s wellbeing and safety
Place2Be – resources and support for families
West Sussex Mind – information and support for mental health
NHS Every Mind Matters – practical tips for wellbeing
You can also speak to your GP or access local services such as the Chichester Family Hub or CAMHS .
Looking After Yourself
Supporting a child can sometimes feel challenging. Looking after your own wellbeing is important too.
Reach out for support when you need it
Take time to rest and recharge
Talk to someone you trust
You are not alone - support is always available.
Getting Help
If you have any concerns about your child’s wellbeing, please contact the school. We are here to listen and work with you to ensure every child feels:
Our Senior Mental Health Lead is Mrs Katie Hoebee who can be contacted directly at head@funtingtonprimaryschool.co.uk

Welcome
A very warm welcome to the Funtington Primary School website.
We are a small and friendly learning community set in beautiful grounds at the foot of the South Downs National Park. Our caring ethos puts the children at the centre of all we do to ensure we support them to develop academically, socially and emotionally. We have a committed team of staff and governors who are passionate about nurturing each individual through a culture of caring, safety and high expectations so that every child can achieve their best. We place high value on children’s personal development and are constantly seeking to broaden their experiences and teach them skills to keep safe, happy and healthy. Our fantastic parent body actively supports the work of the school through volunteer work and fundraising as well as organizing fantastic events that bring the whole community together.
Our aim is to build strong relationships with all our children and families to secure a happy learning community that is always ‘Moving Forward, Loving Learning’
We are always happy to meet prospective parents and children, so if you would like to come and see us in action, please contact the school office.
I look forward to welcoming you to our school.
Vision & Values
Our school vision has been developed through consulting with staff, governors, children and parents and is underpinned by the Funtington Footprints, which make up our core values.
‘A nurturing community which provides a caring, supportive and inclusive environment that sets high expectations and values all members of the school.’
Confidence
To create a community where everyone can feel valued and believe in themselves. To support each child to be an INDEPENDENT learner.
Community
To create an inclusive environment where diverse members of the school community feel a sense of belonging. We nurture mutual RESPECT, strong friendships and teamwork.
Success
To inspire and encourage everyone to aim high in a life-long love of learning. To value and celebrate individual strengths and promote a wide range of experiences in and out of the classroom so children can achieve their BEST.
Learning
To work together with enthusiasm and PERSEVERENCE to engage in a creative, inspiring and purposeful curriculum. To develop enquiring minds who are equipped to make a positive contribution to life beyond the classroom.
Caring
To create a CARING school community that promotes emotional, mental and physical wellbeing where everyone can feel positive about themselves and others. We work together to respect our school and local environment and know how to keep ourselves and others SAFE.
The Funtington Footprints
To take responsibility for my own learning and behaviour.
To know that my actions affect those around me.
To find my own solutions to problems.
To respect other people’s views and to take turns.
To respect our school and belongings and to put things away.
To be polite and use good manners.
To use equipment safely and not to hurt others with words or actions.
To keep myself safe by regulating my emotions.
To keep trying hard with our learning and our friendships even when things get really hard.
To challenge myself and those around me to do better.
To be kind, helpful and friendly to others.
To look out for each other and treat others how we would like to be treated.
To always do my best, help others do their best and to work as a team member.
